html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. API: application programming interface; JSON: JavaScript Object Notation; MCP: Model Context Protocol; SDK: software development kit

  • A requirement-to-answer chooser for every domain
  • The names, values and rules that questions use
  • The distractor patterns and the rule that defeats each

2Decision Chooser

D2 Applications and Integration (33.1%)

If the requirement is... The best answer is... Module
Waiting user Realtime Messages API; stream for perceived speed 2, 3
Non-urgent bulk work, cost first Message Batches API (50% off, up to 24 h, custom_id) 3
Same long prefix on every call Prompt caching: stable first, volatile last; check usage 3
Hard reasoning vs routine requests Effort by task (adaptive thinking); manual budget_tokens rejected 3
429 Back off, retry-after, lower concurrency 3, 16
4xx Fix the request 3, 16
Existing cloud contract and IAM Claude through that cloud platform 3
Behavior differs by interface The interface adds instructions: recreate them in the API request 4
Reproducible behavior Pin model ID, version prompts, commit settings 4
Business goal to build target Functional, non-functional, infrastructure requirements with measurable criteria 1

D1 Agents (14.7%), D5 Models (16.8%)

If the requirement is... The best answer is... Module
Steps known and must be reliable Workflow (chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer) 5
Path depends on discoveries Agent (tool-use loop) 5
Verbose work flooding context Subagent (isolated context, summary returns) 5, 9
Long-running async, little infrastructure Managed Agents 6
Execution must stay in our cloud Self-hosted sandbox 6
A rule that must always hold Hook or permission rule 6, 14
Volume classification Haiku-tier model verified by evals 8
Unsure, balanced Start with Sonnet or Opus; step up when evals fail 8
Reduce cost safely Cache, batch, route, lower effort, prune; verify with evals 8
Output differs run to run Sampling is random: constrain with prompts, structure, evals 7

D6, D8, D7, D3, D4

If the requirement is... The best answer is... Module
Late-session drift and bloat Prune tool output, compact, isolate, fresh session 9
Vague, inconsistent output Specific criteria, format, few-shot examples; iterate with evals 10
JSON fails to parse Structured output / strict schema + defensive parsing 10
Plausible wrong values Validate against the source; shape is not truth 10
Wrong tool chosen Better description and schema first 11
Sensitive tool action Validation + approval gate + idempotency 11
Capability shared by many apps MCP server 12
Procedure or expertise on demand Skill (progressive disclosure) 12
One app's logic Custom tool 12
stdio MCP server breaks Do not write to stdout; log to stderr 12
Hidden instructions in content Untrusted data: separate, tag, least privilege, screen 13
Never run X PreToolUse hook / deny rule 14
Key leaked Revoke, rotate, remove from history, review usage 14
Team standards in Claude Code Committed project CLAUDE.md and .claude/settings.json 4, 15
Script or CI run claude -p; stream-json for progress 15
Wrong answers Check what the model actually received; replay the request 16
Exam tip

Read the last sentence of the item first, name the binding constraint (latency, cost, security, reliability), then match it to a row of this chooser.

3Names and Values to Know

Item Value
Messages API max_tokens required; system is separate; stateless; stop_reason: end_turn, max_tokens, stop_sequence, tool_use, pause_turn, refusal
Streaming events message_start, content_block_start/delta/stop, message_delta, message_stop, ping, error
Caching 5 min or 1 h; write ~1.25x (5 min), read ~0.1x; up to 4 breakpoints; minimum size; cache_read_input_tokens
Batch 50% off; up to 24 h; custom_id; no mid-request tool loop
Effort low, medium, high, xhigh, max; fast mode speed: "fast"
Errors 400, 401, 403, 404, 413, 429, 500, 504, overloaded; SDK retries twice by default
Tools name, description, input_schema; tool_use → tool_result; is_error
MCP tools, resources, prompts; stdio (stderr logging) and HTTP
Settings user, shared project (.claude/settings.json), local, managed
Keys sk-ant-; shown once; secrets manager; rotate
Exam tip

Exact names matter: max_tokens, stop_reason, cache_control, custom_id, input_schema, tool_result, .mcp.json, -p.

4Distractor Patterns

Distractor Why it is wrong
Parallel realtime calls for a cost problem Does not lower the per-token price
"Always the largest model" / "always the smallest" Model must meet a measured bar at the lowest cost
Raising temperature or switching to a bigger model for security Not security controls (and sampling parameters are unsupported on current models)
A polite request in the prompt to stop attacks Not enforceable
Hard-coding shared logic into prompts Not reusable or maintainable
Trusting confident output Validate and verify
Rewriting the prompt for an HTTP error The failure is in the integration layer
Keys in code or the browser Secrets belong in a secrets manager on the server
Exam tip

A distractor is wrong because it is probabilistic, unenforced, over-engineered, over-privileged or aimed at the wrong layer.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Study order D2 first (33.1%), then D5, D1, D6, D8, D7, then D3 and D4
Core stance Match API to latency · model to task · cache stable prefixes · untrusted content stays data · enforce in code · validate output · locate the failure · keep context lean · reuse through the right mechanism · secrets out of code
Day before Reread this module and the ten rules in Module 0
